sections.h2: What is the Town of Palm Tree, New York?
sections.html:
Palm Tree is one of the newest towns in New York, created on January 1, 2019 in Orange County and covering exactly the same land as the village of Kiryas Joel. It was carved out of the Town of Monroe after a referendum on November 7, 2017, and the state legislature moved the start date up by a year in 2018. In 2019 residents also voted for a single town-village government that runs like a village (Wikipedia).

The town measures only 1.5 square miles, with land area of 1.46 square miles in the 2020 census, and almost none of it is water apart from a small pond in the center. That compact footprint gives it about 22,540 people per square mile. The census counted 32,954 residents in April 2020, and the Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 47,147, a rise of 43.1 percent from the 2020 base.

For a seller, the practical point is that older paperwork, tax maps and deeds may refer to Monroe or to the village, while current records use Palm Tree. Make sure your deed, tax bill and any survey describe the same parcel.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Palm Tree housing?
sections.html:
Palm Tree's households are large, and only a third of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The Census Bureau counted 7,505 households with 5.08 people each on average, an owner-occupied rate of 33.4 percent, a median owner-occupied value of $758,800 and median gross rent of $1,604 (QuickFacts).

  • Median monthly owner costs: $2,616 with a mortgage and $1,075 without
  • Residents under 18: 55.2 percent, and under 5: 18.4 percent
  • Residents 65 or older: 2.4 percent
  • Median household income: $50,032 in 2024 dollars
  • Mean travel time to work: 18.9 minutes
  • Residents in the same house a year earlier: 95.3 percent

A buyer's appraiser will look at how each unit in a house is used, so gather floor plans, unit counts and rent figures before you ask for offers.

sections.h2: Where are Palm Tree deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Palm Tree are recorded with the Orange County Clerk in Goshen. The Record Room is at 255 Main Street on the second floor of the Government Center, and the clerk keeps deeds, mortgages, satisfactions of mortgage, federal tax liens, judgments and lis pendens (Orange County Clerk Record Room).

  • The public may use office computers at no charge to search records, and an online search site is available.
  • Plain copies cost $0.65 per page with a $1.30 minimum, and certified copies cost $1.25 per page with a $5.00 minimum.
  • The clerk says a copy of your own deed costs about $5 and warns against companies that charge a fee to fetch one.
  • A free Fraud Alert service emails owners when a deed or mortgage is recorded under their name (County Clerk).

Search for judgments and liens against your name before you list. A seller who finds one early can arrange the payoff, and the title search will turn it up anyway.

sections.h2: How are Palm Tree property taxes collected and challenged?
sections.html:
Orange County publishes a general schedule, and the town tax collector gives the exact one. The county's assessor and collector page lists collection periods by type of bill, shown below, and tells owners to contact their municipality's tax collector for a precise schedule (Orange County).

Type of tax billUsual collection period in Orange County
County and townJanuary through March
SchoolSeptember through November
VillageJune through October

Source: Orange County Assessors page.

Because Palm Tree and Kiryas Joel are the same territory, ask the tax collector which of these bills apply to your parcel. Questions about delinquent taxes and penalties go to the county finance office at 845-291-2480.

For assessment challenges, the state tax department says Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May in most communities, and it tells owners to confirm the date with the local assessor (tax.ny.gov). The complaint is filed on Form RP-524 with the assessor or the board of assessment review, it costs nothing, and only the current tentative roll can be grieved. Palm Tree's grievance date for the coming year is a question for its assessor.

sections.h2: How much state transfer tax does a Palm Tree seller owe?
sections.html:
The state charges $2 for every $500 of the price, rounded up to the next $500, and the seller pays it unless the contract says otherwise (tax.ny.gov). At the town's median owner-occupied value of $758,800, the rounded price is $759,000, which is 1,518 units and $3,036.

The Combined Real Estate Transfer Tax Return, Form TP-584, is filed with the county clerk, and the form and tax are due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. A residence sold for $1 million or more also carries the 1 percent mansion tax, paid by the buyer.

One rule matters for investors. When a limited liability company is the buyer or seller of a building with up to four dwelling units, the state will not accept the transfer return unless it comes with the names and addresses of all members, managers and other authorized persons. If a member is itself a company, the list continues until natural persons are identified. Gather that information before the closing date.

sections.h2: What disclosures apply when a Palm Tree house has tenants?
sections.html:
The seller of a one to four family house must hand the buyer a signed property condition disclosure statement before the buyer signs a binding contract (Real Property Law 462). The law leaves room for as-is sales, and the form is not a warranty.

Question 4 asks whether anyone other than the owner holds a lease, easement or other right to use or occupy part of the property. With an owner-occupied rate of 33.4 percent, many Palm Tree buyers will ask about leases and rents right away, so collect copies and the rent roll before you list. The form also covers certificates of occupancy, shared walls or driveways, flood zones, water and sewage service, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and the condition of the roof, heating and plumbing.

The town and village governments were combined, so ask Palm Tree town hall which office issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for your address. Get that answer in writing if work on the house was done in the past.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a fit for a Palm Tree property?
sections.html: A cash offer can suit an owner who wants a short timeline, a house with deferred repairs or a building with occupied units. Without a lender, the closing depends on payoffs, a clear title search and recording in Goshen. Request the offer in writing, confirm who pays each transfer cost, and have a New York attorney read the contract before you sign.

faqs.q: Is Palm Tree the same place as Kiryas Joel?
faqs.a: Their boundaries are identical. The town of Palm Tree was created on January 1, 2019 and is coterminous with the village of Kiryas Joel, which had been part of the Town of Monroe. Your deed may name either one, so check which description your title company uses.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Palm Tree house?
faqs.a: The Orange County Clerk in Goshen. The Record Room is at 255 Main Street, second floor of the Government Center. The office also offers a free Fraud Alert that tells owners when a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a $759,000 Palm Tree sale?
faqs.a: It is $3,036 at the state rate of $2 per $500. The seller normally pays it, and the buyer pays the 1 percent mansion tax only when the price reaches $1 million. Form TP-584 and the tax go to the county clerk within 15 days of the deed's delivery.

faqs.q: When does Orange County collect county and town taxes?
faqs.a: Generally from January through March, with school taxes collected from September through November. The county says exact periods vary by municipality, so the Palm Tree tax collector has the final schedule for your bill.

faqs.q: Do I have to tell a buyer about tenants in my Palm Tree house?
faqs.a: Yes, the disclosure form asks whether anyone other than you has a lease or right to use or occupy any part of the property. Answer from your own knowledge, attach extra pages if needed, and give the form to the buyer before the contract is signed.
